title: Maximize Score of Numbers in Ranges
summary: Given an array of start points and a distance d for n intervals, select n integers such that the i-th integer is within the i-th interval [start[i], start[i] + d].
statement: Given an array of start points and a distance d for n intervals, select n integers such that the i-th integer is within the i-th interval [start[i], start[i] + d]. The score is the smallest absolute difference between any two chosen integers. Determine the highest achievable score.
constraints: start contains 2–100,000 interval starts; every selectable interval is [start[i],start[i]+d].
Choose one integer from every interval and score the minimum absolute difference among choices.
reference_solution:
def maximum_interval_choice_spacing(start,d):
    intervals=sorted(start)
    def possible(gap):
        chosen=intervals[0]
        for left in intervals[1:]:
            chosen=max(left,chosen+gap)
            if chosen>left+d:return False
        return True
    low=0;high=intervals[-1]+d-intervals[0]
    while low<high:
        middle=(low+high+1)//2
        if possible(middle):low=middle
        else:high=middle-1
    return low

Sort intervals and greedily choose each value as early as possible while respecting the candidate gap.
Set chosen=max(interval start, previous+gap); fail if it exceeds start+d.
The earliest feasible choice leaves maximal room for all later intervals, so greedy feasibility is exact and monotone.
